extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications industry stakeholders, FCC counsel, technical engineers, and public interest parties participating in 5.9 GHz band rulemaking (ET Docket No. 19-138)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used by the FCC to evaluate petitions for reconsideration and technical coexistence analyses regarding the redesignation and technical rules for the 5.850-5.925 GHz band (ET Docket No. 19-138). Includes legal authority, interference protections, measurement procedures, and technical assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redesignation of the lower 45 megahertz for unlicensed use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may repurpose spectrum (here, removing the lower 45 megahertz from ITS use and making it available for unlicensed operations) when deployment evidence and public-interest analysis support doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision justified by minimal DSRC deployment over 20 years, availability of other technologies and bands to provide many automotive safety functions, cost-benefit/public-interest analysis in the First Report and Order, and the conclusion that 30 megahertz is sufficient to serve ITS safety needs. The Commission found retaining the entire 75 MHz unnecessary when future ITS uses are uncertain or remote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority under 47 U.S.C. 316 for modifying authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications to existing ITS authorizations (e.g., transitioning operations to a different portion of the band) must be within the Commission's statutory authority under 47 U.S.C. 316 and consistent with prior Commission practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission concluded the modification was well within its authority, consistent with precedent, and serves the public interest, convenience, and necessity. Legal objections that the Commission exceeded authority require persuasive legal grounds to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect incumbents from harmful interference via operating and power limits
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect incumbent 5.9 GHz services (including federal incumbents and ITS), the Commission may impose stringent power limits and operating requirements on unlicensed devices operating in adjacent spectrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include restricting unlicensed use of the lower 45 MHz to indoor locations, setting specific power/OOBE limits for access points, subordinate devices, and client devices, and relying on building attenuation and path loss to limit interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: OOBE limits for the upper 30 MHz based on U-NII-3 limits plus building-attenuation adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Out-of-band emissions (OOBE) limits allowed in the upper 30 MHz for indoor unlicensed operations in the lower 45 MHz are based on, but not identical to, the previously-affirmed OOBE limits for unlicensed operations in the 5.725-5.850 GHz (U-NII-3) band, increased to account for building attenuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission increased the allowed OOBE into the upper 30 MHz by an additional 20 dB compared to U-NII-3 OOBE limits, reasoning that indoor restriction and building attenuation justify the relaxed limit so that it mirrors U-NII-3 after accounting for building loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of RMS detector for OOBE measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: RMS (root mean square) detection is permitted to conduct all 5.9 GHz band unlicensed device OOBE measurements instead of requiring peak detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RMS measurement is preferred because it represents continuous power (better reflecting interference potential) while peak measurements capture infrequent short-duration peaks. The Commission found RMS more appropriate to minimize interference risk and to promote flexible measurement techniques for shared spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity factor (duty cycle) assumption for unlicensed device interference analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses of interference potential should use an activity factor (percentage of time a device transmits) grounded in measurement data; the Commission used 0.4% based on prior 6 GHz order and 5 GHz U-NII router measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a higher assumed activity factor (e.g., 2%) can substantially overestimate average transmitted power (approx. 7 dB over-estimation). Parties' coexistence studies should use measurement-based activity factors consistent with Commission precedent unless justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: OBU transmit power assumptions per existing technical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses should use the transmit-power limits applicable under current rules and referenced technical standards (e.g., 47 CFR 95.3189 and IEEE 802.11p-2010) when assessing interference to OBUs (on-board units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under IEEE 802.11p-2010 (as referenced in 47 CFR 95.3189), OBUs operated by entities other than state/local governments may use up to 33 dBm EIRP; using a lower power value (e.g., 20 dBm) in coexistence analyses can under- or mischaracterize interference scenarios and is inappropriate without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of building attenuation, path loss, and antenna pattern effects in interference assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Interference analyses must account for factors such as building attenuation, separation distance (path loss), and directionality/angular discrimination of receiving antennas (e.g., C-V2X OBU antenna orientation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission found that building attenuation, path loss due to separation, and the horizontal orientation/directionality of C-V2X antennas provide isolation that reduces received OOBE power. Studies that ignore these factors (e.g., assuming zero dB average antenna gain) are deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for judicial and administrative deference to Commission technical judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: The court will uphold the Commission's technical judgments if supported with a modicum of reasoned analysis; petitioners must present highly persuasive evidence to the contrary to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative assertions or analyses that fail to address the Commission's stated technical reasoning (e.g., building attenuation, path loss, antenna discrimination, measurement choices) are unlikely to overturn the Commission's determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to reserve spectrum for speculative future technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission need not retain spectrum for 'yet-to-arrive technologies' that are too uncertain or remote to warrant reservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectrum allocation decisions can be based on current and reasonably foreseeable technologies; speculative future benefits do not, by themselves, justify holding spectrum in reserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform OOBE measurement policy across equipment types where previously adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying a consistent OOBE requirement for equipment operating in a band (as the Commission did in 2016 for U-NII-3) is an acceptable approach; differentiation among equipment types is not required absent a reasoned basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission previously elected to provide 'a single, consistent OOBE requirement for all equipment' in U-NII-3; extending the same basis to U-NII-4 equipment is appropriate unless a party demonstrates why different treatment is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural thresholds for RFA, PRA, and CRA applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations about whether a regulatory action triggers the Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA), Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA), or Congressional Review Act (CRA) depend on whether new final rules or new/modified information-collection obligations are promulgated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Order on Reconsideration promulgates no additional final rules (so not an RFA matter), contains no new or modified information collection requirements (so not subject to PRA burdens), and will not be sent to Congress under CRA because no rule was adopted or amended in this Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition requirement for ITS licensees to upper 30 MHz
rubrics_metrics.description: ITS licensees are required to cease operations on channels in the lower 45 MHz and move to channels in the upper 30 MHz within one year of the effective date of the First Report and Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission also updated ITS service rules to facilitate transition from DSRC to C-V2X during a transition period determined through the FNPRM record. Compliance timelines and protocol-transition plans are part of the implementation framework.
